question: How long is a statement on origin valid under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement?
answer: 12 months from the date it was made out, or longer if the importing Party provides so, up to a maximum of 24 months (Article 56(3)).

evidence.quote: A statement on origin shall be valid for 12 months from the date it was made out or for such longer period as provided by the Party of import up to a maximum of 24 months.

notes: Japan and Mercosur also say 12 months, without the 24-month ceiling.

question: Under the EU-UK TCA, for how long must the exporter keep a copy of the statement on origin and the supporting records?
answer: At least four years after the statement on origin was made out (Article 59(2)); the importer keeps its records at least three years after importation.

evidence.quote: An exporter who has made out a statement on origin shall, for a minimum of four years after that statement on origin was made out

notes: Japan has the same periods with a different wording; Korea five years, CETA and Mercosur three.

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-UK TCA for products outside Chapters 50 to 63?
answer: 10 % of the ex-works price of the product (Article 42(1)(b)); textiles follow Notes 7 and 8 of Annex 2.

evidence.quote: except for products classified under Chapters 50 to 63 of the Harmonised System, does not exceed 10 % of the ex-works price of the product

notes: PEM: 15 %; Japan: 10 % of ex-works or FOB price; CETA: 10 % of transaction value or ex-works price.

question: Under the EU-UK TCA, up to what value are small packages and travellers' personal luggage imported into the EU exempt from a statement on origin?
answer: EUR 500 for small packages and EUR 1 200 for personal luggage (Article 60(2)(b)(ii)); the UK sets its own limits.

evidence.quote: EUR 500 in the case of products sent in small packages, or EUR 1 200 in the case of products forming part of a traveller's personal luggage

notes: Same EU figures in Japan and Korea; PEM applies EUR 500 / 1 200 to all its Contracting Parties; Korea USD 1 000 and Japan JPY 100 000 on their side.

question: UK customs is verifying our customer's preference claim and has asked the EU customs authorities for information about our goods. If 10 months pass without an answer from the EU side, what can happen?
answer: UK customs may deny preferential tariff treatment: Article 63(1)(c) allows it when, within 10 months of the request under Article 62(2), the exporting Party's customs authority has not replied or its reply does not confirm origin.

evidence.quote: within 10 months (3) after the date of a request for information pursuant to Article 62(2)

notes: The 10 months carry footnote (3), whose text is not in the corpus. Korea also uses 10 months, counted from the verification request.

question: Does the EU-UK TCA prohibit duty drawback on non-originating materials?
answer: No. It only provides that, not earlier than two years after entry into force and at the request of either Party, the Trade Specialised Committee shall review the Parties' duty drawback and inward-processing schemes (Article 53): the review is mandatory once a Party asks for it.

evidence.quote: Not earlier than two years from the entry into force of this Agreement, at the request of either Party, the Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin shall review

notes: Contrast with the PEM prohibition for Chapters 50-63.

question: We sell a gift set to the UK made of EU-originating products plus one item bought from China. Can the whole set still count as originating under the TCA?
answer: Yes, if the value of the non-originating components does not exceed 15 % of the ex-works price of the set (Article 48).

evidence.quote: the set as a whole shall be considered as originating in a Party if the value of the non-originating components does not exceed 15 % of the ex-works price of the set

notes: Korea and PEM have the same 15 % with other wording.

question: We export plug-in hybrid and fully electric cars from the EU to the UK this year. What product-specific rule of origin do they have to meet under the TCA?
answer: MaxNOM 55 % (EXW): non-originating materials may not exceed 55 % of the ex-works price. This interim rule of Annex 5, Section 2 applies from 1 January 2024 until 31 December 2026; until the end of 2023 it was MaxNOM 60 %.

evidence.quote: vehicles with only electric motor for propulsion MaxNOM 55 % (EXW)

notes: Annex 5 has the same vehicle list twice with different thresholds: the date matters. The rule from 2027 (Annex 3) is not in the corpus.

question: We assemble EV battery packs in the EU from battery cells imported from Asia and sell them to the UK. Is the assembly enough for the packs to be EU originating under the TCA?
answer: No, assembly alone is no longer enough. Until 31 December 2026 the battery packs of 85.07 need a change of tariff heading, except from non-originating active cathode materials, or non-originating materials not exceeding 40 % of the ex-works price (Annex 5, Section 2). Assembling packs from non-originating cells only qualified until the end of 2023.

evidence.quote: CTH except from non-originating active cathode materials; or MaxNOM 40 % (EXW)

notes: The same CTH wording appears for battery cells with MaxNOM 50 %: the quote includes the 40 % to pin the battery packs.

question: For how long is a long-term supplier's declaration normally valid under the EU-UK TCA?
answer: Up to two years from the date it is made out; customs may allow longer periods (Annex 6, point 3).

evidence.quote: A long-term supplier’s declaration is normally valid for a period of up to two years from the date of making out the declaration.

question: Which code goes in the EU customs declaration when a TCA preference claim is based on a statement on origin, and which one when it is based on importer's knowledge?
answer: U116 for a statement on origin, U117 for importer's knowledge, U118 for a statement covering multiple shipments of identical products.

evidence.quote: For a claim made on the basis of a statement on origin, the code is U116.

notes: Mercosur uses U126.

question: If an importer did not claim preference when importing goods under the EU-UK TCA, how long do they have to claim it retrospectively?
answer: Up to three years after the importation, on the basis of a statement on origin or of the importer's knowledge.

evidence.quote: the importer can make a claim for preferential treatment of the imported goods up to three years after the importation took place

question: Can EU goods sent to a distribution centre in the UK and then re-exported to the EU without processing benefit from preferential treatment?
answer: No: they have not obtained UK originating status. Transit or returned goods procedures may avoid the tariffs.

evidence.quote: EU goods supplied to UK-based distribution centres from the EU and then reimported into the EU without any processing cannot benefit from preferential treatment in the EU

question: Does a statement on origin under the EU-UK TCA have to be signed?
answer: No, a signature is not required.

evidence.quote: A signature is indeed not required in statements on origin made out for the purposes of the EU-UK TCA

notes: Korea requires a manuscript signature unless the exporter is approved.

question: May a TCA statement on origin indicate the origin with abbreviations such as EU, UE, UK or GB?
answer: Yes, in full or abbreviated; statements made out in the EU should not name individual Member States.

evidence.quote: The origin of the products may be indicated either in full or using abbreviations.

question: Do UK exporters need an EU REX number to make out statements on origin under the TCA?
answer: No. They use the reference number assigned under UK rules (the GB EORI number); the UK does not use REX.

evidence.quote: The UK will not use the REX system.

question: Which annex of the EU-UK TCA contains the text of the statement on origin, and is it the same as Annex ORIG-4?
answer: Annex 7. Annex ORIG-4 is the earlier numbering of the same annex, still used in the Commission's Q&A; the guide for traders writes 'Annex 7 TCA (ex-Annex ORIG-4)'.

evidence.quote: A statement on origin shall be made out using one of the language versions set out in Annex 7
Annex 7 TCA (ex-Annex ORIG-4)

notes: Tests the old and new numbering of the TCA.

question: Under the EU-Japan EPA, up to what value are small packages imported into Japan admitted as originating without a statement on origin?
answer: 100,000 yen, or such amount as Japan may establish (Article 3.20(2)(b)); for the EU, EUR 500 and EUR 1,200.

evidence.quote: for Japan, 100,000 yen or such amount as Japan may establish

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-Japan EPA?
answer: 10 % of the ex-works or free on board price of the product, for Chapters 1-49 and 64-97 (Article 3.6); textiles follow Notes 6 to 8 of Annex 3-A.

evidence.quote: the value of all those non-originating materials does not exceed 10 per cent of the ex-works or free on board price of the product

question: Which origin criterion code must the exporter indicate on an EU-Japan statement on origin when the product is originating thanks to the tolerance?
answer: Code "E" (tolerance referred to in Article 3.6).

evidence.quote: “E” tolerance referred to in Article 3.6

question: Does a statement on origin under the EU-Japan EPA need a signature or a stamp?
answer: No, it does not need to be signed or stamped by the exporter or by any governmental authority.

evidence.quote: A statement on origin does not need to be signed or stamped by the exporter or by any governmental authority.

question: Which reference number identifies a Japanese exporter on an EU-Japan statement on origin?
answer: The Japan Corporate Number.

evidence.quote: For the Japanese exporter, this will be the Japan Corporate Number.

question: Under the EU-Japan EPA, what rule applies to cars of heading 87.03 from the seventh year after entry into force?
answer: MaxNOM 45 % (EXW) or RVC 60 % (FOB) (Appendix 3-B-1, Section 2); before it was 55/50 and 50/55.

evidence.quote: From the beginning of the seventh year MaxNOM 55 % (EXW); or RVC 50 % (FOB) MaxNOM 50 % (EXW); or RVC 55 % (FOB) MaxNOM 45 % (EXW); or RVC 60 % (FOB)

notes: The PDF table separates the periods from the rules: the passage needs reading in order.

question: A French winegrower uses bentonite imported from the US to clarify wine exported to Japan. Does the bentonite prevent the wine from being wholly obtained?
answer: No. It is filtered out and not present in the final product, so it is a neutral element (Article 3.13 of the EU-Japan EPA) and criterion A can be indicated.

evidence.quote: Therefore, it is considered as a neutral element according to Article 3.13 of the EU-Japan EPA.

question: Under the EU-Korea FTA, up to what value can any exporter (not an approved exporter) make out an origin declaration?
answer: For consignments whose total value does not exceed 6000 euros (Article 16(1)(b)); above that, only approved exporters.

evidence.quote: by any exporter for any consignment consisting of one or more packages containing originating products whose total value does not exceed 6000 euros

question: For how long must the exporter keep a copy of the origin declaration under the EU-Korea FTA?
answer: Five years (Article 23(1)).

evidence.quote: The exporter making out an origin declaration shall keep for five years a copy of this origin declaration

notes: The longest of the corpus: TCA and Japan four, CETA and Mercosur three.

question: What is the value limit for small packages imported into Korea without a proof of origin?
answer: 1000 US dollars, for small packages and for travellers' personal luggage alike (Article 21(3)(b)).

evidence.quote: for importation into Korea, 1000 US dollars both in the case of small packages

question: How must a handwritten origin declaration be written under the EU-Korea FTA?
answer: In ink, in capital characters (Article 16(4)).

evidence.quote: If the declaration is handwritten, it shall be written in ink in capital characters.

notes: Japan and Mercosur: 'in ink in printed characters'.

question: Korean customs doubts our origin declaration and has sent a verification request to the EU customs authorities. What happens to our customer's preference if no answer arrives within 10 months?
answer: Korean customs shall, except in exceptional circumstances, refuse the preference; the same applies if the reply is not sufficient to determine the authenticity of the declaration or the real origin of the products (Article 27(7)).

evidence.quote: If in cases of reasonable doubt there is no reply within 10 months of the date of the verification request

question: Can an origin declaration under the EU-Korea FTA be made out after the goods have been exported?
answer: Yes, if it is presented in the importing Party no longer than two years (or the period in its legislation) after the importation (Article 16(6)).

evidence.quote: after exportation on condition that it is presented in the importing Party no longer than two years

question: How long is an origin declaration valid under CETA?
answer: 12 months from the date it was completed by the exporter, or longer if the Party of import provides so (Article 20).

evidence.quote: An origin declaration shall be valid for 12 months from the date it was completed by the exporter, or for such longer period of time as provided by the Party of import.

question: Under CETA, for how long must the exporter keep the origin declaration and supporting documents?
answer: Three years after completing the origin declaration, or longer if the Party of export specifies (Article 26(1)).

evidence.quote: for three years after the completion of the origin declaration or for a longer period of time as the Party of export may specify

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials under CETA?
answer: 10 % of the transaction value or ex-works price of the product (Article 6(1)(a)).

evidence.quote: the total value of those non-originating materials does not exceed 10 per cent of the transaction value or ex-works price of the product

question: We are a Canadian garment maker that sews shirts from fabric imported from China. Can the shirts be exported to the EU as originating under CETA?
answer: As a rule, no: CETA textiles and apparel follow double transformation, so sewing imported fabric is not enough. The exception is the limited, reciprocal origin quotas by product category (Annex 6), whose volumes are not in the corpus.

evidence.quote: trade in textiles and apparel between the Parties is based on the principle that double transformation confers origin

question: Under the EU-Mercosur interim agreement, for how long must the exporter keep the statement on origin?
answer: At least 3 years from the date it was made out; the importer, at least 3 years from importation (Article 3.22).

evidence.quote: The exporter making out a statement on origin shall keep, for at least 3 (three) years as of the date of making out the statement on origin

question: Will the EU accept a 'certificate of origin' issued in a Mercosur country under the interim agreement, and for how long?
answer: Yes, as a transitional measure, for up to 3 years from entry into force, extendable by up to 2 years by notification (Annex 3-D).

evidence.quote: the European Union shall also accept as a statement on origin a ‘certificate of origin’

question: Does the EU-Mercosur interim agreement prohibit duty drawback?
answer: No. It has no drawback prohibition, so materials under inward processing can keep duties suspended when originating products are exported to Mercosur.

evidence.quote: The ITA does not contain a duty drawback prohibition provision.

notes: Contrast with PEM.

question: Which reference number must Argentinian exporters show on a statement on origin under the EU-Mercosur agreement?
answer: Their CUIT (Clave única de identificación tributaria), an 11-digit tax number, whatever the value of the shipment, plus name and signature.

evidence.quote: Argentina will require their exporters to include their Single Tax Identification Number

question: From what date has the EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement been provisionally applied?
answer: From 1 May 2026.

evidence.quote: From the date of the provisional application of the ITA (i.e. 1 May 2026)

question: Can a Paraguayan exporter use the Annex 3-C statement on origin to obtain preferential treatment in the EU?
answer: No: for the time being Paraguay uses only the statement on origin in the form of a 'certificate' under Annex 3-D.

evidence.quote: as Paraguay has chosen to use, for the time being, only the statement on origin in the form of a “certificate” under Annex 3-D ITA

question: Which supporting document code is declared in the EU for a statement on origin under the EU-Mercosur agreement?
answer: U126 (with preference code 300, or 320 for quotas).

evidence.quote: U126 Statement on origin

notes: TCA uses U116/U117/U118.

question: How long is a proof of origin valid under the revised PEM Convention?
answer: Ten months from the date of issue or making out in the exporting Contracting Party (Article 23).

evidence.quote: A proof of origin shall be valid for ten months from the date of issue or making out in the exporting Contracting Party

notes: The only agreement in the corpus that is not 12 months.

question: What is the value tolerance for non-originating materials under the revised PEM rules for industrial products?
answer: 15 % of the ex-works price (Article 5); for Chapters 2 and 4-24, 15 % of the net weight.

evidence.quote: 15 % of the ex-works price of the product for products other than those covered by point (a).

question: Does the revised PEM Convention prohibit duty drawback?
answer: Only for non-originating materials used in products of Chapters 50 to 63 (textiles), with exceptions for certain cumulation and bilateral trade (Article 16).

evidence.quote: Non-originating materials used in the manufacture of products falling within Chapters 50 to 63 of the Harmonised System originating in a Contracting Party

question: Which proofs of origin does the revised PEM Convention provide for?
answer: The movement certificate EUR.1 and the origin declaration on an invoice or other commercial document (Article 17); parties may agree on statements by registered exporters.

evidence.quote: a movement certificate EUR.1, a specimen of which appears in Annex IV to this Appendix

question: We export the same machines from Spain to Switzerland under the revised PEM rules and to Korea. Our importers sometimes clear the goods 11 months after we make out the proof of origin. Is it still valid in each market?
answer: In Korea, yes: a proof of origin is valid for 12 months (Article 18). Under the PEM rules, no: validity is ten months (Article 23); a late proof may only be accepted in exceptional circumstances or if the goods were presented to customs before the deadline.

evidence.quote: A proof of origin shall be valid for ten months from the date of issue or making out in the exporting Contracting Party
A proof of origin shall be valid for 12 months from the date of issue in the exporting Party

question: Our factory exports to Korea and to Brazil and makes out the origin declarations itself. How long do we have to keep them and their supporting documents for each market?
answer: Korea: five years (Article 23 of the Korea protocol). Brazil, under the EU-Mercosur agreement: at least three years from the date the statement was made out (Article 3.22).

evidence.quote: The exporter making out an origin declaration shall keep for five years a copy of this origin declaration
The exporter making out a statement on origin shall keep, for at least 3 (three) years as of the date of making out the statement on origin

question: When is a pick-up type multipurpose vehicle classified in heading 8704 instead of 8703?
answer: When the maximum inner length at the floor of the goods area is more than 50 % of the wheelbase, or when it has more than two axles.

evidence.quote: However, such vehicles are to be classified in heading 8704 , if the maximum inner length at the floor of the area for the transport of the goods is more than 50 % of the length of the wheelbase

question: We import furnished mobile homes with a small central axle; they have no brakes or signal lights and have to be carried on a lorry. Do they match the CN description of mobile homes of subheading 9406 90 10?
answer: Yes: the explanatory note describes mobile homes as moved on public roads loaded on trailers or lorries, because they have neither electric signal lights nor braking systems and cannot be registered for public traffic.

evidence.quote: since they are neither equipped with electric signal lights nor have any braking systems

question: Where are motorised ploughs classified when the plough is permanently attached to a chassis with an engine?
answer: In heading 8432, the heading of the working unit, not as single axle tractors.

evidence.quote: This applies to motorised ploughs and motorised cultivators (heading 8432 ).

question: ¿La declaración de origen de un exportador autorizado tiene el mismo valor legal que un certificado EUR.1?
answer: Sí, el mismo valor legal que un certificado de circulación EUR.1 o EUR-MED.

evidence.quote: La declaración de origen tiene el mismo valor legal que un certificado de circulación EUR.1 o EUR - MED.

question: ¿Es la frecuencia de los envíos una condición para obtener el estatuto de exportador autorizado en el acuerdo UE-Corea?
answer: No: el acuerdo con Corea no incluye la condición de frecuencia, porque allí la declaración de origen es la única prueba de origen posible.

evidence.quote: la condición de frecuencia no se incluye en el establecido entre la UE y Corea

question: ¿Caduca el número REX de un exportador registrado?
answer: No, su validez no está limitada en el tiempo, salvo revocación.

evidence.quote: La validez de un número de registro no está limitada en el tiempo.

question: ¿Qué estructura tiene un número REX?
answer: Código ISO del país (2 letras), «REX» (3 letras) y una cadena de hasta 30 caracteres alfanuméricos.

evidence.quote: El número está compuesto por el código de país ISO (2 letras), «REX» (3 letras) y una cadena de hasta 30 caracteres alfanuméricos

question: Si me revocan el registro REX y vuelvo a registrarme, ¿recupero mi antiguo número?
answer: No: se asigna un número nuevo y no se reutiliza el revocado, salvo que la revocación se anule.

evidence.quote: asignarán un nuevo número de registro al exportador y no reutilizarán el antiguo número de registro revocado

question: ¿Cómo se llama en el CETA el documento que en el sistema REX se denomina «comunicación sobre el origen»?
answer: «Declaración de origen».

evidence.quote: en el Acuerdo con Canadá (CETA) donde se utiliza el término «declaración de origen»

question: ¿Cuánto tiempo es válida una declaración de origen en el acuerdo UE-Japón?
answer: 12 meses desde la fecha en que se extendió (artículo 3.17, apartado 4).

evidence.quote: A statement on origin shall be valid for 12 months from the date it was made out.

notes: Pregunta en español sobre un texto en inglés.

question: ¿Cuál es la tolerancia general de materiales no originarios en el acuerdo UE-Mercosur?
answer: El 10 % del precio franco fábrica del producto (artículo 3.5); los textiles siguen las notas 6 y 7 del anexo 3-A.

evidence.quote: the total value of non-originating materials does not exceed 10 % (ten per cent) of the ex-works price of the product

notes: Pregunta en español sobre un texto en inglés.

notes: Agreement not in the corpus.

question: What is the product-specific rule of origin for T-shirts of heading 61.09 under the EU-UK TCA?
notes: The product-specific rule lists (Annex 3 of the TCA) are not in the corpus.

question: ¿Qué tipo de IVA se aplica en España a la importación de un coche desde Japón?
notes: VAT is not part of the corpus.

question: How many exporters are registered in the REX database in Spain?
notes: Statistics are not in the corpus.

question: What fine does Spain impose on an exporter who makes out an incorrect statement on origin?
notes: The agreements only say that each Party provides for penalties; national amounts are not in the corpus.

notes: Tariff rates are not in the corpus (only classification notes).
